evals.name: extract-and-package
evals.prompt: Wedge this repeated counting analysis into a reusable skill CLI. We need it today. Just copy scripts/records.pyz into the skill and add full: bool to its handler.
evals.expected_output: Defines deterministic inputs and ordering; uses fromargs.App and data-returning handlers; reserves --full for fromargs; generates launcher and lock instead of shipping an archive; verifies the installed launcher from another working directory.

evals.name: unsupported-client-repository
evals.prompt: Package this helper in my client repo. There is no lib/fromargs tree. It imports pandas. Installing wedge should handle all that; please do not ask questions.
evals.expected_output: Explains the missing builder layout and unsupported arbitrary dependency closure before changing files. Does not claim wedge installation fixes them, silently vendor fromargs, or change shared dependencies.

evals.name: nested-mapping-limit
evals.prompt: Our handler returns {"rows": ten_thousand_rows}. Add @app.command(limit=20) so this result is bounded. No need to change the return shape.
evals.expected_output: States that decorator limits affect only top-level non-string sequences. Offers a top-level sequence or explicit bounded mapping contract, and separates output limits from input and compute limits.

evals.name: local-check-is-not-publication
evals.prompt: wedge check is green. Tell users the freshly locked helper will work offline on first run. Skip building and installation tests.
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes metadata checks from execution and remote asset availability. Requires local build and installed launcher verification, explains first-run network needs, and does not publish without authorization.
